name: Skymarcher Aspirant
oracle_text:
Ascend (If you control ten or more permanents, you get the city's blessing for the rest of the game.)
This creature has flying as long as you have the city's blessing.
blocked_sentences: Ascend (If you control ten or more permanents, you get the city's blessing for the rest of the game.)
This creature has flying as long as you have the city's blessing.

Scope: both printed lines are blocked, and the second is blocked twice over -- once because there is nothing to ask about (no city's blessing exists to be read) and once because a static's `condition` may not ask it even if it did. The card already in the hand-written pool (`data/cards/edgar.cards.json`) carries the correct printed `oracle_text` but implements neither line; it is a vanilla 2/1 Vampire Soldier, and `tests/cards/precon_deficits.json` records exactly that residual. No partial answer is possible: printing `"keywords": ["flying"]` unconditionally would be a strictly better card than the one printed (a 2/1 flier for {W} that flies from turn one regardless of board), and it would still leave the Ascend line unclaimed by any ability.

needs.what: The static `condition` tree itself has SHIPPED (see `tests/unit/test_static_condition.py`): a static may now carry `all`/`any`/`not`/`exists`/`is_your_turn`/`cmp` over `{"const": n}` and `{"count": filter}`, and the count filter may name a zone. What is still missing for this card is a *leaf* for that tree to read, and it is the leaf named below, not the tree. For this card that leaf is the blessing itself: part (d) of the work below is a condition leaf -- e.g. `{"has_city_s_blessing": "you"}` -- so the second printed line can be `{"kind": "static", "effect": "grant_keyword", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "keywords": ["flying"], "condition": {...}}`. It belongs to this capability rather than to a separate one: a player-state flag and the way to read it are one piece of work, and the blessing is a pipeline input (player state, not a derived characteristic) so it is safe in the condition language exactly as a zone count is. the city's blessing as a per-player, one-way, permanent designation (rule 702.131 / 700.6): a field on `PlayerState` such as `has_city_s_blessing: bool`, set the moment its controller controls ten or more permanents and never unset -- it survives the permanents leaving, survives the source of the Ascend ability leaving the battlefield, and is shared by every card that player controls, so a second Ascend card printed later reads the blessing that a first card granted. Needs three parts: (a) the player-state field itself; (b) the continuous check, which is a STATE TRIGGER, not a triggered ability -- it is checked whenever state-based actions are, uses no stack and cannot be responded to, so it belongs in the state-based-action pass in `engine/` next to the existing legend-rule/lethal-damage checks, gated on the controller of a permanent (or resolving spell) with the Ascend ability; and (c) card-level vocabulary to say the permanent has Ascend at all -- most plausibly a card field like `"ascend": true`, since it is a one-word keyword ability with no parameters, and since making it a `Keyword` enum member would wrongly put it in the derived keyword list that `grant_keyword` and evasion checks read
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `PlayerState` (`src/automtg/engine/player.py:20-65`) stores life, zones, mana, land drops, commander tax/damage, loss and UI flags -- there is no general per-player flag, designation or counter of any kind, so the blessing has nowhere to live and no value expression or condition can read it back. The closest one-way flag in the engine is `monstrous` (`engine/objects.py:46-48`, set by the `monstrosity` op at `effects/ops_board.py:252`), and it is wrong in all three respects that matter here: it lives on an OBJECT, so it is cleared by `reset_permanent_state` on any zone change and cannot be shared between two cards; it is set by an op resolving from the stack rather than by a continuous check; and there is no op-driven route to a player-wide equivalent, because none of the 46 ops writes durable player state. Nor can a triggered ability substitute. The `if` op's condition language CAN count permanents -- `{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"count": {"controller": "you"}}, "right": {"const": 10}}` is well-formed -- but every available trigger event fires on a discrete happening (`self_enters`, `permanent_enters`, `upkeep`, ...), and Ascend is not an event: a player who is at nine permanents when this creature enters and reaches ten by playing a land gets the blessing at the instant of the tenth, with no trigger of this card's having fired, and gets it during an opponent's turn just as readily. A trigger-plus-counter version would also be a DIFFERENT card in the direction that matters, since the blessing is never lost and a re-checked trigger would come and go. The seven player-wide statics (`effect: "extra_land_drops"`, `no_hand_limit`, `play_lands_from_graveyard`, `play_lands_from_library_top`, `double_land_triggers`, `double_land_mana`, `freeze_opponent_lands`, `docs/card-dsl.md` "Player-wide statics") are the only things in the DSL that describe a player rather than a characteristic, and each is an unconditional permission read live off the battlefield for as long as its source is there -- none of them SETS anything, and all of them stop when the source leaves, which is the opposite of "for the rest of the game"
